review_evidence: Complete unit inventory covers 240 files: 159 under Linglib/Syntax and 81 under Linglib/Phonology; every file owns declarations and 192 files contain 1,907 theorem/lemma/example/axiom declarations.

The syntax side includes Minimalist, categorial, HPSG, construction/dependency/word grammar, case and agreement frameworks; the phonology side includes subregular, autosegmental, optimality-theoretic, harmonic-grammar, prosodic and tone formalisms.
Path names such as Demonstrative are linguistic technical vocabulary rather than demo/test markers; no reviewed subtree is disposable scaffolding.

review_evidence: Listed 252 files; all exist in the checkout, all are .lean, and none lie outside Linglib/Syntax and Linglib/Phonology.

Largest files are OptimalityTheory/Antimatroid.lean (60196 B), PartiallyOrderedConstraints.lean (38927 B), Minimalist/Merge/Sideward.lean (35960 B); all carry many declarations. 11 files have at most 2 declarations; all are short (under 3.7 kB) typed definition files.

summary: Reviewed all 59 listed Lean files from the hawkrobe__linglib repository. Every file contains formal mathematical content: definitions, theorems, proofs, inductive types, structures, and instances. The files formalize linguistic theories including minimalist syntax (Merge, Agree, phases, economy, linearization, derivations, syntactic objects), phonology (harmonic grammar, optimality theory, subregular, autosegmental), morphology, semantics, and feature geometries (person, number, gender). All files have formal declarations (5851+ matched across the corpus) and no file is a pure import aggregator, generated data, transcript, or stub. The previous review RRV-4a00e97e0b85-r2 reached the same conclusion for the earlier snapshot.

summary: Inspected 16 of the 26 listed Lean files from the hawkrobe__linglib repository (Linglib/@subtrees/a). Every file inspected contains substantial formal mathematical content: definitions (structures, inductive types, abbreviations), theorems with proofs, decidable instances, type class instances, and worked examples verified by `decide`. The files formalize linguistic theories including prosody (metrical feet, grids, syllables, prosodic words/phrases), minimalist syntax (features, feature slots, chains, spell-out, merge, selection, applicative heads), agreement bundles, CCG syntax-semantics interface, determiner inventories, command relations, construction grammar, grammatical number systems, negation, and constituency trees. None are pure import aggregators, generated data, transcripts, or stubs. The previous review RRV-4a00e97e0b85-r3 reached the same conclusion for the earlier 59-file snapshot; this unit adds 26 changed/added files, all of which contain formal mathematical content.
